key_insight: A thermodynamically constrained surrogate can replace expensive detailed chemistry in reacting-flow DNS while preserving physically admissible evolution and stable time integration.
engineering_relevance: This enables high-fidelity combustion simulation at a fraction of the cost, with accurate transfer to new inlet conditions using synthetic residual-based augmentation.
method: Train a machine-learning surrogate to predict chemical source terms from a reduced thermochemical state.
Enforce non-negative entropy generation during training to satisfy the second law and constrain state evolution.
Use residual-based synthetic data augmentation to expand the training set for parametric generalization without new DNS runs.
evidence_signal: In a 2D planar lean premixed methane-air flame DNS, the surrogate matched detailed-chemistry results closely and reduced computational cost by more than an order of magnitude.
watch_item: Entropy constraints improve physical consistency, but performance may depend on how well the reduced state and synthetic augmentation cover conditions outside the original training regime.
paper_title: Entropy-Constrained Machine Learning with Residual Data Augmentation for Modeling Chemical Kinetics
